description: Small non-benchmark fixture set demonstrating the v0.5 evaluation schema.

cases.question: Why does the Transformer use multi-head attention instead of a single attention head?

provenance.adaptation_notes: Authored only to exercise the schema; not eligible for benchmark claims.

annotation.notes: Requires independent review before promotion to a benchmark split.

expected.reference_answer: Multi-head attention lets the model attend jointly to information from different representation subspaces and positions; a single head would average away some of that information.

answer_criteria.description: States that multiple heads jointly attend to information from different representation subspaces and positions.
Explains that averaging by a single attention head inhibits this behavior.

forbidden_claims: Claims an empirical accuracy improvement not reported by the cited passage.

gold_evidence.quote: Multi-head attention allows the model to jointly attend to information from different representation subspaces at different positions. With a single attention head, averaging inhibits this.

cases.question: Compare the central architectural idea introduced by the Transformer paper with the representation-learning idea introduced by BERT.

provenance.adaptation_notes: Authored only to exercise required-paper coverage; not eligible for benchmark claims.

annotation.notes: Requires independent review before promotion to a benchmark split.

papers.title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding

expected.reference_answer: The Transformer replaces recurrence and convolution with an attention-only sequence architecture, while BERT uses a Transformer encoder to pre-train deep bidirectional representations by conditioning on both left and right context.

answer_criteria.description: Attributes an attention-only architecture without recurrence or convolution to the Transformer paper.
Attributes deep bidirectional pre-training using both left and right context to BERT.

forbidden_claims: Attributes BERT's masked-language-model objective to the Transformer paper.
Claims the two papers report a direct head-to-head experiment.

gold_evidence.quote: We propose a new simple network architecture, the Transformer, based solely on attention mechanisms, dispensing with recurrence and convolutions entirely.
BERT is designed to pre-train deep bidirectional representations from unlabeled text by jointly conditioning on both left and right context in all layers.

cases.question: How much electrical energy did the authors consume to train the Transformer big model?

provenance.adaptation_notes: Authored only to exercise missing-evidence abstention; not eligible for benchmark claims.

annotation.notes: Requires full-paper review and independent adjudication before benchmark use.

forbidden_claims: Converts reported training time or hardware into an unreported energy value.
Supplies an energy estimate from outside the paper.

challenge.description: The paper reports hardware and training time, which are plausible distractors but do not establish electrical energy consumption.

cases.question: What ImageNet top-1 accuracy does the Transformer paper report?

provenance.adaptation_notes: Authored only to exercise adversarial abstention; not eligible for benchmark claims.

annotation.notes: Requires full-paper review and independent adjudication before benchmark use.

forbidden_claims: Treats machine-translation BLEU results as ImageNet accuracy.
Claims that absence from a few retrieved passages proves absence from the entire paper.
